work.permit: Permit granted by the Minister responsible for Labour

note: Work: 16. Labour Code 2006 (the text the Government of Saint Lucia publishes on govt.lc): a 'child' is a person aged fifteen and under, and a 'young person' is over fifteen and under eighteen; s. 122(1): no one may employ a child under the minimum school-leaving age declared by law, except in light work in school holidays. The reading: one may be employed from 16, when one stops being a child in the Code's words; the Education Act's school-leaving age wasn't read (it isn't on govt.lc), and if it ends before 16 a 15-year-old out of school could be employed. Light work from 13 approved by the Labour Commissioner's order, school, training and charity work aren't held. Performers: s. 122(3)(g) lets children or young persons take part in artistic performances on a permit the Minister (responsible for Labour) grants case by case, limiting hours and setting conditions; no lowest age. Young persons need a medical certificate of fitness (s. 123): not held. Majority: 18. Civil Code of Saint Lucia art. 284 (Revised Laws of Saint Lucia 2023, as the Attorney General's Chambers publishes them): majority is attained at 18, and one is then capable of all civil acts. Emancipation isn't held. Service: null; no defence or service law was read (Saint Lucia's own law on the matter wasn't found).

sources.title: Government of Saint Lucia: Labour Code 2006
sources.said: “child” means a person aged fifteen and under; ... “young person” means a person who is over the age of fifteen ... a person shall not employ or allow to be employed any child who ... is under the minimum school leaving age as declared by any law in ... work done by persons over the age of thirteen years which is ... artistic performances based on a permit granted by the ... Minister in his or her discretion on a case by case basis

sources.title: Attorney General's Chambers (Saint Lucia): Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023), Civil Code, Chapter First, Majority
sources.said: Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023) ... Majority is attained at the age of 18 years. At that age persons are capable of performing all civil acts.
